bugs.title: int ** negative int exponent truncates i64 exponent to i32
bugs.description: pow_vals negative-exponent path calls fpowi(ai as f64, exp as i32). The `as i32` cast wraps for exponents outside i32 range (inline ints go to ±2^47), so e.g. -4294967296 becomes 0 and fpowi returns 1.0.

bugs.title: 0 ** negative and 0.0 ** negative return inf instead of raising ZeroDivisionError
bugs.description: pow_vals: `0 ** -1` goes through fpowi(0.0, -1) = 1.0/0.0 = inf; `0.0 ** -0.5` goes through fpowf -> libm::pow = inf. Python raises ZeroDivisionError for 0 to a negative power.
bugs.expected: ZeroDivisionError: 0.0 cannot be raised to a negative power

bugs.title: Non-empty format spec on a float with no precision renders fixed-6 instead of str()
bugs.description: apply() ty==0 branch routes a float with a non-empty spec but no precision into format_float(v, s, b'f', heap), whose default precision is 6. Python formats with str(float) semantics when no type/precision is given, only applying alignment/width/sign.

bugs.title: Format spec on a container renders as empty string (padding only)
bugs.description: format_value -> apply() ty==0 falls through to display_inline(), whose fallback for non-scalar heap objects (list/tuple/dict/set/...) is String::new(). So f"{[1,2]:>10}" produces 10 spaces. Python applies the spec to str(value).

bugs.title: repr/str of a user function is malformed: '<function 0' (no name, no closing '>')
bugs.description: display_d for HeapObj::Func builds s!("<function ", int *i) — it prints the raw function-table index and never closes the angle bracket.
bugs.expected: something well-formed like '<function foo>' (Python: '<function foo at 0x...>')

bugs.title: bytes + bytes and bytes * int are unsupported (TypeError)
bugs.description: add_vals has no (Bytes, Bytes) concatenation arm and mul_vals' repetition arm only accepts Str/List/Tuple, so b"ab" + b"cd" and b"\xff" * 3 raise TypeError. Python supports both.
bugs.actual: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'bytes' and 'bytes'

bugs.title: bool as sequence-repetition count is rejected (True * [1,2] raises TypeError)
bugs.description: mul_vals repetition requires b.is_int() (inline int) and explicitly skips LongInt; bool is neither, so True * [1,2] and 'x' * True fail. Everywhere else bool unifies with int (as_i128 handles it). Python: True * [1,2] == [1,2].
bugs.actual: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'bool' and 'list'

bugs.title: int.from_bytes silently truncates values wider than i128
bugs.description: from_bytes accumulates with (acc << 8) | b on i128 with no overflow check; bits shifted past bit 127 are silently dropped. A 17-byte input returns a wrong small value instead of raising.
bugs.expected: an OverflowError (engine ints cap at i128) — certainly not 0

bugs.title: float/LongInt equality contradicts hashing: equal values, different hashes
bugs.description: eq_vals_depth compares float vs LongInt via num_as_f64 (lossy f64 rounding), so 1e16 == 10**16+1 is True (Python: False — it converts the float exactly). But hash_depth hashes the integral float as i64(1e16) and the LongInt as i64(10^16+1): different hashes for 'equal' values. Dict/get and ValSet operations disagree: d={1e16:'x'}; d.get(10**16+1) misses while 10**16+1 in {1e16} is True (contains uses a linear eq scan) and {1e16} & {10**16+1} is empty (ValSet uses hashes).
bugs.expected: Python: False / 'missing' / False — i.e. Python says not-equal so the miss is consistent; here eq says equal but the dict still misses, which is an internal invariant violation either way

bugs.title: next() on a plain list mutates it (removes the front element)
bugs.description: call_next accepts any heap List and does v.remove(0) on the caller's list (list.__next__ does the same). Python raises TypeError: 'list' object is not an iterator. The design intends this for iter() results, but iter() returns a fresh list anyway, so the destructive path only bites user-owned lists.
bugs.expected: TypeError: 'list' object is not an iterator (Python); at minimum xs must not be mutated

bugs.title: pow(a, b, mod) with negative modulus returns positive result
bugs.description: call_pow takes modulus.unsigned_abs() and uses rem_euclid, so pow(2, 3, -5) returns 3. Python's three-arg pow returns a result with the sign of the modulus: pow(2, 3, -5) == -2.

bugs.title: Bytes literals don't decode octal escapes (b"\101" stays literal)
bugs.description: parse_bytes_literal handles \xHH and a single \0, but multi-digit octal like \101 falls into the `other` arm which keeps the backslash verbatim. String literals decode octal correctly (push_escape), bytes don't.

bugs.title: time.time_ns() returns a str, not an int
bugs.description: The time_ns binding allocates HeapObj::Str(now_ns().to_string()) while its siblings monotonic_ns/perf_counter_ns correctly produce ints via int_val. type(time.time_ns()) is <class 'str'>.

bugs.title: strptime %y maps 69-99 to 2069-2099 instead of 1969-1999
bugs.description: time_strptime does `'y' => y = 2000 + v` unconditionally. Python (and POSIX) maps 0-68 -> 2000-2068 and 69-99 -> 1969-1999. Same bug in the JS twin web/builtins/time/src/fmt.js:57.

bugs.title: math.isqrt(i128::MAX) returns a huge negative number
bugs.description: isqrt starts y = (x + 1) / 2 with x = n; for n = i128::MAX the x+1 overflows. In release builds it wraps and the Newton loop converges to -2^126; in debug it panics. (2^127-1 is representable as an Edge int, e.g. (2**126 - 1) * 2 + 1.)

bugs.title: math.gcd(i128::MIN) returns a negative gcd
bugs.description: gcd/lcm call i128::abs(); for i128::MIN (-2^127, reachable as (-2**126) * 2) abs() wraps to itself in release (panics in debug), so gcd returns -2^127 and lcm computes garbage.

bugs.title: math.log(x, 1) returns inf instead of raising
bugs.description: The two-arg log guards base <= 0.0 but not base == 1.0, so it computes ln(x) / ln(1) = ln(x) / 0.0 = inf. Python raises ZeroDivisionError.
bugs.expected: ZeroDivisionError (Python: 'float division by zero' from log base 1)

bugs.title: math.floor/ceil/trunc reject exactly -2^127 though it fits i128
bugs.description: to_int rejects x.abs() >= 2^127 symmetrically, but i128::MIN is exactly -2^127 and is representable. floor(-170141183460469231731687303715884105728.0) wrongly raises.
bugs.actual: ValueError: int too large to convert

bugs.title: math.pow(0.0, -1.0) returns inf; overflow returns inf instead of raising
bugs.description: pow uses nan2! which only maps NaN results to 'math domain error'. libm::pow(0.0, -1.0) is inf (not NaN), so no error; Python raises ValueError. Likewise pow(1e308, 2) -> inf where Python raises OverflowError.

bugs.title: math.comb reports overflow for results that fit in i128
bugs.description: comb multiplies the accumulator by (n - k + i) before dividing by i, so the intermediate can exceed i128 even when the final result fits. E.g. comb(13128212440888706149, 2): true result ~8.6e37 < 2^127, but acc=(n-1) then *n overflows.
bugs.actual: ValueError: comb() result exceeds the i128 range

bugs.title: math.hypot overflows/underflows: no scaling
bugs.description: hypot sums v*v directly, so hypot(1e308, 1e308) = inf (v*v overflows) where Python returns 1.4142135623730951e+308; tiny inputs similarly underflow to 0.0. The comment claims it matches math.hypot(*coordinates).

bugs.title: json.loads accepts invalid JSON numbers (leading zeros, trailing dot)
bugs.description: read_number doesn't enforce JSON's number grammar: loads("01") returns 1 and loads("1.") returns 1.0. Both are rejected by Python's json.loads and by the JSON spec.

bugs.title: Numeric backreference to a nonexistent group compiles and matches empty
bugs.description: \\1 in a pattern with no groups parses to Node::Backref(1) with no validation; matcher treats the missing slot as an unmatched (empty) group. Python raises 'invalid group reference 1' at compile time; the std/re README also promises invalid patterns raise ValueError.
bugs.actual: matches the empty string at position 0 (prints a blank match)

bugs.title: FFI float encode does not canonicalize NaN (tag-space collision)
bugs.description: classify_encode returns EncodeRequest::Direct(f64::from_le_bytes(buf).to_bits()) without the CANON_NAN mapping Val::float performs (src/value/mod.rs:92). A plugin encoding a NaN whose bits collide with the tag space (e.g. 0x7FFC_0000_0000_0001 == TAG_NONE) injects a Val the VM reads as None/int. Reasoning-confirmed from code; reaching it needs a hand-written wasm plugin returning such NaN bits.
bugs.repro: wasm plugin calls edge_encode(tag::FLOAT, bits=0x7FFC000000000001); the Python side receives None instead of nan
bugs.actual: NaN payload bits reinterpreted as tag values (None/int)
bugs.expected: canonical NaN, same as Val::float produces internally

bugs.title: Plugin __call__ with >= 256 args wraps the packed Call operand
bugs.description: operand = args.len() as u16 is decoded by parse_call_args as lo byte = positional count, hi byte = kw pairs. argc = 256 wraps to operand 0x0100 = 0 positional + 1 kw pair, desyncing the VM stack. No arity guard on the FFI path.
bugs.repro: plugin does Handle::call("__call__", argv) with argv.len() >= 256
bugs.actual: wrong argc decoded; stack desync / garbage results
bugs.expected: either a clean arity error or correct dispatch

bugs.title: FFI Op::Len / Op::Iter reject bytes handles
bugs.description: dispatch_len and dispatch_iter have no HeapObj::Bytes arm, although in-language len(b'..') works and bytes are iterable (iter_to_vec handles them). A plugin calling len/iter on a bytes handle gets 'object of type bytes has no len()' / 'is not iterable'. Also falsifies the 'flatten any iterable' comment on dispatch_iter.
bugs.repro: plugin: edge_op(Len, bytes_handle) or edge_op(Iter, bytes_handle)
bugs.expected: byte length / list of ints, matching in-language semantics

bugs.title: limits_of() discards the recorded op budget and reports ops: 1
bugs.description: The snapshot blob stores the remaining budget; limits_of reads it (let _budget = r.usz()?) then returns ops: 1 for sandboxed snapshots, contradicting its doc 'Sandbox profile recorded at save time'. Currently masked because both callers re-read the budget inside restore(); any other consumer gets a wrong profile.
bugs.repro: save a snapshot with sandbox limits, inspect via limits_of()
bugs.expected: the budget recorded at save time

bugs.title: devkit JSON parser rejects valid \b and \f escapes
bugs.description: Cursor::string() handles \" \\ \/ \n \t \r \uXXXX only; spec-valid \b and \f produce 'unsupported escape'. This parser feeds the native network builtins, so third-party JSON containing \b/\f fails to parse.
bugs.repro: native network binding receives a JSON payload containing \b or \f

bugs.title: edge build re-ingests the previous dist/ output (skip guard never fires)
bugs.description: walk() skips the output dir via `if path == out_dir { continue; }`, but out_dir is the bare relative 'dist' while read_dir(".") yields './dist' — Path equality preserves the leading './', so the guard never matches. Second and later builds collect the stale dist/*.py (and vendored test.py) and copy them to dist/dist/..., growing the output each build.
bugs.repro: edge build twice in a project whose scripts import the test package (or with any dist/ present)
bugs.actual: dist/dist/... appears; script count inflates per build
bugs.expected: dist/ is excluded from collection on every build

bugs.title: `import a, b` only vendors package `a`
bugs.description: crawl_imports breaks after the first token of an import line, so for `import a, b` the second module is never recorded and not vendored into dist/; the bundled app fails to resolve `b` at run time.
bugs.repro: project with 'import json, re' at top level, then edge build

bugs.title: find_entry returns bare 'main.py' for a nested match, breaking the generated index.html
bugs.description: The preferred-name loop checks s.file_name() == c but then returns the bare constant c. If the only main.py is at sub/main.py, index.html points at dist/main.py which does not exist (the file was copied to dist/sub/main.py).
bugs.repro: project whose only entry candidate is sub/main.py, then edge build

bugs.title: edge add with a .py URL misclassifies a std package as a host library
bugs.description: kind_from_url only treats .wasm as std, so `edge add test=https://example.com/test.py` lands in the host map even though std packages shipped as pure .py are explicitly supported (manifest.rs special-cases test; build.rs preserves .py when vendoring Kind::Std). The runtime then loads a Python file as a main-thread JS library.
bugs.expected: entry under std/imports, mirroring the .py handling in build.rs

bugs.title: Piped stdin keeps trailing \r on CRLF input
bugs.description: The native session splits piped stdin on '\n' only, so each input() line from CRLF sources (Windows pipes/files) ends with '\r', diverging from Python's input() semantics.

bugs.title: Live-reload fingerprint truncates mtimes to whole seconds
bugs.description: The watch fingerprint sums d.as_secs() (and sizes). An edit within the same second that keeps total size identical produces the same fingerprint, so the page never reloads — plausible with the 400ms poll.
bugs.repro: edge serve; save a same-byte-length fix-up twice within one second
bugs.expected: reload on any content change (use as_millis/nanos or hash per file)

bugs.title: Uninstall writes a script to a predictable world-writable temp path
bugs.description: std::env::temp_dir().join("edge-uninstall.sh") + fs::write follows pre-existing symlinks, letting another user on a shared machine pre-plant a symlink and have the uninstalling user overwrite an arbitrary file they own.
bugs.actual: victim's file is overwritten with the uninstall script

bugs.title: pause() reports 'parked' but only PREEMPTED yields actually hold the program
bugs.description: settlePause(true) fires at the top of the drive loop for every yield kind, but the resumeGate await exists only in the STATUS_PREEMPTED branch. For PENDING_TIMER/FRAME/HOST_CALL the driver services the yield and calls run_resume() — the program keeps running after pause() resolved true. A pause during a long sleep() is also only noticed after the timer fires. Contradicts the pause doc in web/src/index.js:122 and the README.
bugs.repro: program with sleep(5); call pause() from the host; it resolves true yet the program continues after the sleep
bugs.actual: pause() resolves true but execution continues on the next serviced yield

bugs.title: IndexedDB cache wiped on every page load when version is omitted (the default)
bugs.description: `if (!version || stored !== version) { await cache.clear(); }` — version defaults to null (and element.js never passes one), so !version is always true and the persistent cache is cleared on every createWorker, making it useless across page loads. README documents invalidation only on version mismatch.
bugs.repro: createWorker without a version; reload the page; cache is empty again
bugs.expected: cache persists; cleared only when a provided version mismatches

bugs.title: Synthetic root packages.json shadows a physical one
bugs.description: Whenever the resolution table is non-empty, prefetch does fetchedSources.set('packages.json', synthetic). The walk-up then finds 'packages.json' already cached and never fetches the real file, silently dropping its imports/host/extends for programmatic runs with entryDir=''.
bugs.repro: programmatic run with a real root packages.json next to the entry plus any imports
bugs.actual: the physical packages.json is never fetched
bugs.expected: synthetic defaults merge with, not replace, the physical manifest

bugs.title: Cross-origin worker bootstrap failure hangs createWorker forever
bugs.description: On dynamic-import failure the blob bootstrap posts { type: 'error', message: 'worker bootstrap failed: ...' } with no reqId; the main-thread handler does pending.get(data.reqId) -> undefined and returns early, so the send('load') promise never settles and no onerror fires.
bugs.repro: embed cross-origin with an unreachable CDN URL
bugs.actual: createWorker() promise never resolves or rejects

bugs.title: strptime with an unknown month name silently rolls back to December of the previous year
bugs.description: monthIndex('Foo') returns -1, so mo = -1 + 1 = 0 and Date.UTC(Y, -1, d) normalizes to December of year Y-1 instead of raising 'does not match format'. Out-of-range %m/%d fields similarly normalize instead of erroring.
bugs.expected: time data ... does not match format error

bugs.title: ws_close(h, None) throws InvalidAccessError instead of a clean close
bugs.description: Python None arrives as JS null, but the guard is `code !== undefined`, so ws.close(null, '') runs; WebIDL coerces null to close-code 0, which is invalid and throws. Every other optional-arg handler in web/builtins/ also treats null as absent.
bugs.repro: ws_close(h, None) from Python in the web runtime

bugs.title: match cannot take a parenthesized subject
bugs.description: The lexer demotes the soft keyword `match` to a Name when followed by Lpar (lines 90-99), so `match (1, 2):` lexes as a call and the parser errors. Python accepts a parenthesized subject.

bugs.title: Set -= rebinds instead of mutating in place
bugs.description: There is no InPlaceSub opcode; only InPlaceBitOr/And/Xor are handled (dispatch.rs:628). `s -= x` rebinds s to a new set, so aliases keep the old value. |=, &=, ^= mutate correctly.

bugs.title: Format spec 'n' rejects floats
bugs.description: The 'n' type routes through int_to_decimal_parts, which requires an integer, so f"{1234.5:n}" raises. Python applies locale-unaware grouping to floats and prints 1234.5.
bugs.actual: ValueError: format spec requires an integer

bugs.title: type_name returns 'object' for every user instance
bugs.description: Error messages never name the user's class. Surfaced at dispatch.rs:830: `with AC(): pass` on a class without the protocol reports 'object' instead of 'AC'.
bugs.repro:
class AC:
  pass
with AC():
  pass
bugs.actual: TypeError: 'object' object does not support the context manager protocol
bugs.expected: TypeError: 'AC' object does not support the context manager protocol

bugs.title: __iter__ returning a built-in iterator is silently treated as empty
bugs.description: __next__ is probed via try_call_dunder (opcodes/dunder.rs:157-171, 185), which only works on user Instances; a miss is treated as end of iteration. A class whose __iter__ returns iter([1,2,3]) iterates as empty and `in` returns False.

bugs.title: gather re-raises the last error in time, not the first in argument order
bugs.description: raise_into_outer reuses self.pending.exc_val (the most recently raised exception) instead of building one from the error it was handed, defeating the deliberate first-in-argument-order first_err pick at line 281.
bugs.repro:
async def bad1():
  raise ValueError("from bad1")
async def bad2():
  raise ValueError("from bad2")
try:
  await gather(bad1(), bad2())
except ValueError as e:
  print("caught:", e)
bugs.actual: caught: from bad2 (whichever coroutine errored last in time)
bugs.expected: caught: from bad1 (first in argument order, per the code's own intent at line 281)

bugs.title: int() rejects the string form of i128::MIN
bugs.description: The magnitude is parsed with i128::from_str_radix, which rejects 2^127, and the sign is applied after, so the one representable negative extreme fails while its positive sibling parses.

bugs.title: Keyword arguments break when a builtin is called through an alias
bugs.description: dispatch_native rejects kwargs for every builtin except Sorted, bypassing the kwarg handling in call_print, call_minmax, call_enumerate, and call_dict that the dedicated opcodes reach on a direct call.
bugs.actual: TypeError: native function takes no keyword arguments

bugs.title: import_module() NameError message is doubly wrapped
bugs.description: A full sentence is passed into VmErr::Name, whose renderer wraps it again as name '<X>' is not defined, producing nested quoting.
bugs.actual: NameError: name 'module 'json' not imported in this scope' is not defined
bugs.expected: NameError: module 'json' not imported in this scope

bugs.title: MemoryError from a full heap is uncatchable
bugs.description: Entering an except handler allocates (the message string and the ExcInstance, via heap.alloc at dispatch.rs:236-241). When the heap is exhausted that allocation re-fails and the error propagates past the handler. A MemoryError raised by a pre-flight size check IS caught, confirming the mechanism.
bugs.actual: MemoryError: heap limit, exit code 1 (handler never runs)
bugs.notes: Also misformatted on the way out: the uncaught MemoryError prints bare to stdout instead of the normal 'error: ... --> file:line' stderr format other uncaught errors use.

bugs.title: hash() does not unify value-equal numerics
bugs.description: call_hash hashes floats by their raw f64 bits while ints hash as themselves, so 1 == 1.0 but hash(1) != hash(1.0), violating the hash/eq contract at the user level. Related to bug-009 (the internal hash_depth in value/eq.rs has its own float/LongInt disagreement).

bugs.title: User-defined __delitem__ corrupts subsequent method dispatch on the instance
bugs.description: After `del s[key]` runs a user __delitem__, any later method call or `in` check on the instance fails with AttributeError: 'object' object has no attribute '<attr>'. The deletion itself works. Plain del obj.attr and del list[i] are unaffected.

bugs.title: str() of a bare AssertionError returns the class name instead of an empty string
bugs.description: str(AssertionError()) is 'AssertionError' instead of ''. Side effect: the std test harness prints 'FAIL - name (AssertionError: AssertionError)' with the class name doubled for a bare failed assert.

bugs.title: json.dumps of a native module function raises a bogus NameError
bugs.description: Serializing a native function (e.g. dumps itself) raises NameError: name 'dumps' is not defined, while a user-defined function correctly raises TypeError: 'function' is not JSON-serializable.
bugs.repro:
from json import dumps
print(dumps({"fn": dumps}))

bugs.title: Op-limit RuntimeError is effectively uncatchable
bugs.description: When the operation budget runs out, the except handler is entered but its first operation re-raises because the budget stays exceeded. Possibly by design, but the docs do not state it. Also takes ~33 s to trigger under the CLI at the sandbox budget.
bugs.actual: the error re-raises inside the handler (caret lands on the print)
bugs.expected: either 'caught' or a documented uncatchable-error note

bugs.title: Unbounded parser recursion in the call/subscript/method chain overflows the stack and aborts the process
bugs.description: The MAX_EXPR_DEPTH guard in expr_bp (expr.rs:71-88, types.rs:7) catches nested operator/paren/list expressions but not nested calls, subscripts, or method calls. The cycle parse_atom -> call -> parse_args_body -> comma_list -> name -> call (literals.rs:362,486,489,509) recurses after expr_bp already decremented expr_depth, so depth never accumulates across argument nesting and there is no other guard. MAX_INSTRUCTIONS does not help since each level costs about 3 instructions. Because release sets panic = abort a stack overflow is a hard SIGABRT, not a catchable panic, and it happens at parse time before the sandbox op/heap/call budgets run. Confirmed with a compiled proof of concept, about 4800 deep on an 8 MB stack and about 600 on a 1 MB worker thread.
bugs.repro: f(f(f(f(f(f(x))))))  # scale the nesting, or a.m(a.m(a.m(a)))
bugs.actual: thread has overflowed its stack, fatal runtime error, aborting (exit 134)
bugs.expected: a parse error at a fixed nesting depth, like the [[[...]]] case, never a crash

bugs.file: src/vm/value_ops.rs (display_d, instance repr fallback; grep 'instance>' for the exact line)
bugs.title: repr of bare object() omits the class name and prints <instance>
bugs.description: The default __repr__ fallback formats '<ClassName instance>' and user classes follow it (print(Foo()) gives '<Foo instance>'), but for object() the class name reaches the fallback empty and the output is '<instance>'. CPython prints '<object object>'. Possibly related to bug-045 (type_name returns 'object' for every user instance): both suggest the object type has no usable name in the repr/type_name path. Cosmetic and deterministic. Pinned by a verified cell in skill/SKILL.md (json.dumps with default=str of object()), so fixing it will intentionally break that cell and force a doc update.
bugs.expected:
<object instance>
<Foo instance> (CPython prints '<object object>' for the first line)

outdated_comments.comment_says: /* `int(s, base)` parsing: optional sign, optional 0x/0o/0b prefix ... */ placed directly above round_int_banker
outdated_comments.code_does: round_int_banker rounds ints to -k digits; the comment describes parse_int_radix two functions below (line 59). Misplaced comment.
the native hook is SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) (src/native/mod.rs:33), wall-clock since epoch, not a monotonic Instant

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'Fits in 47-bit inline range' (also line 173 '47-bit signed', and src/value/mod.rs:42 '47-bit int')
outdated_comments.code_does: INT_PAYLOAD_MASK is 48 bits (0x0000_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF) with sign extension (raw << 16) >> 16, giving a 48-bit two's-complement range [-2^47, 2^47-1]; '47-bit' reads as ±2^46

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'Python hands list[tuple] but wasm-pdk has no new_tuple (the hook can tuple(p) for p in pairs if it needs them)'
outdated_comments.code_does: Handle::new_tuple exists now (pdk/src/lib.rs:583) and is already used by std/math/src/float.rs:197; the stated constraint is gone
naive sum-of-squares with no scaling; hypot(1e308, 1e308) overflows to inf where math.hypot returns 1.414e308 (see bug-021)

outdated_comments.comment_says: compare_dunder_names returns '(forward, reflected, negate)'; '__ne__' is negated '__eq__'
outdated_comments.code_does: negate is false for every opcode including NotEq; the actual __ne__ fallback (negate __eq__) lives in try_compare_dunder lines 104-108, so the negate field/branch is dead

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'Re-applied at every run since resetNativeTable clears them.'
outdated_comments.code_does: hostImportMap(registerHost, incremental) deliberately skips re-registration in incremental/REPL mode (engine.js:131-132, 209)
the function returns null on any network failure or non-ok status (fetch.js:23-32), not just 404
code coerces any non-finite duration (isFinite check), including Infinity from live streams, to 0

outdated_comments.comment_says: doc on `pub fn run`: 'Write a raw stdout chunk (byte-stream...) and flush so streaming output appears at once.'
outdated_comments.code_does: run writes nothing itself; that sentence describes engine::emit_chunk (engine/mod.rs:23-28). Misplaced leftover doc line

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'Official package registry. Mirrors the runtime's built-in default manifest.' directly above pub enum Kind
outdated_comments.code_does: Kind is just the Std/Host tag; the registry is the registry() function at line 45. Comment sits on the wrong item
the code passes them through verbatim (print(b"\u00e9") gives b'\\u00e9'), and it omits that octal escapes are not decoded either (bug-012)

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'User instance container with __iter__: walk via the iterator protocol'
outdated_comments.code_does: the walk silently returns false/empty when __iter__ returns a non-Instance (built-in) iterator; the miss at line 166 is treated as 'no items' (bug-046)

outdated_comments.comment_says: 'enforce timeouts, then wake any whose tracked tasks are all terminal, finalizing per WaitKind' and the WaitKind::Gather comment at line 477 'raises the first child error'
outdated_comments.code_does: raise_into_outer at lines 321-322 reuses pending.exc_val, so the last error in time wins instead of the first in argument order (bug-047)

outdated_comments.comment_says: call_input 'Returns empty string in sandbox; no stdin access in WASM.'
outdated_comments.code_does: the strict/sandbox path raises RuntimeError and never returns an empty string; the native non-strict path does read stdin

outdated_comments.comment_says: wasm32 error string says 'input() requires host data in WASM (use set_input)'
outdated_comments.code_does: no set_input export exists in src/wasm/exports.rs; the inp buffer is dead surface, so the message points users at a nonexistent API
